note: Narrative journeys for the spiral. Stops are event ids from site/data/events.json in time order; each stop line says what the stop adds, in the record's words.

journeys.title: Bi Sheng to GPT
journeys.line: From baked clay characters set and reused in Song China to a language model answering in prose, text went from what machines set to what machines compose.

stops.line: Bi Sheng's baked clay characters, set in an iron frame and reused, freed each page from being carved as one woodblock.
Gutenberg's metal type, cast in quantity from his hand mould, and his screw press printed about 180 copies of his 42-line Bible by 1455.
Carried by German printers after Gutenberg's monopoly ended, printing reached about 220 presses and 8 million books across Western Europe by 1500.
Sholes and Glidden's typewriter, patented on 23 June 1868, put letters under the fingers; Remington's 1874 production model set essentially today's QWERTY layout.
Herman Hollerith's punched cards let machines count America's 1890 Census months ahead of schedule, after 1880's count had taken eight years.
Alan Turing's 1936 paper described one universal machine that runs any computation from encoded instructions, and used it to prove Hilbert's decision problem has no solution.
An IBM 701 translated more than 60 Russian sentences into English in 1954 using six grammar rules; its authors' five-year forecast failed and funding was cut after 1966.
ELIZA, Joseph Weizenbaum's 1966 program, matched patterns in typed sentences to simulate conversation, and users credited it with understanding it did not have.
Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams's 1986 Nature paper popularised backpropagation, the method by which layered neural networks learn from their errors.
Google's 2017 Transformer reads whole sequences at once and weighs which words bear on each other, beating earlier translation systems by more than 2 points on BLEU, a translation-quality score.
GPT-3, OpenAI's 2020 language model with 175 billion learned parameters, performed translation and question-answering from text prompts and examples alone, with no training per task.
ChatGPT, launched on 30 November 2022 as a free research preview, let anyone converse in writing with OpenAI's GPT-3.5 models.

journeys.title: Telegraph to web
journeys.line: Needle telegraphs patented in 1837 grew, cable by cable and protocol by protocol, into a network that more than half of humanity used by 2018.

stops.line: Cooke and Wheatstone's 1837 telegraph pointed needles at letters, and from 1838 served 13 miles of Great Western Railway track as the world's first commercial telegraph.
Morse's line from Washington to Baltimore, 38 miles Congress funded with $30,000, opened on 24 May 1844 with "What hath God wrought", and his code became telegraphy's worldwide language.
Three weeks after its first official message on 16 August 1858, the first transatlantic cable failed, its insulation damaged by 2,000-volt signalling; durable cable followed in 1866.
On 12 December 1901 Marconi reported hearing Morse's letter S in Newfoundland, sent about 2,200 miles from Cornwall without wires, though historians still debate whether he heard it.
TAT-1, the first transatlantic telephone cable, opened on 25 September 1956 with 35 simultaneous calls and carried 588 London to US calls in its first 24 hours.
ARPANET's first host-to-host message, sent from UCLA to SRI on 29 October 1969, got two letters of "login" through before SRI's machine crashed; its technology became the Internet's foundation.
In May 1974 Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn described a protocol for joining separate networks, which detects lost or disordered packets and reassembles them; it became TCP/IP.
On 1 January 1983, flag day, ARPANET switched from NCP to TCP/IP in one step, and those protocols stayed on for good.
TAT-8, the first transatlantic fiber optic cable, entered service in 1988 carrying 40,000 telephone circuits over glass, far more than copper cables before it, and later early Internet traffic.
In March 1989 Tim Berners-Lee submitted to CERN his proposal for what became the World Wide Web.
NCSA Mosaic, released on 23 January 1993, put graphics and text in one browser window and brought the web to the public.
ITU estimated 51.2 percent of people worldwide, 3.9 billion, were online by end of 2018, more than half of humanity for the first time.

journeys.title: Bubbles and busts
journeys.line: Railway shares in 1846, railroad bonds in 1873, Nasdaq in 2000 and AI capital in 2026, compared against Gartner's hype cycle, a framework rather than any measurement.

stops.line: UK railway shares peaked in 1846, when Parliament passed 263 railway acts, then collapsed after the Bank of England raised rates, leaving about one third of authorised lines unbuilt.
Jay Cooke & Company failed in September 1873 when it could not sell Northern Pacific Railway bonds, setting off chain bank failures and the Long Depression.
Record trading of 12.9 million shares on Black Thursday and 16.4 million on Black Tuesday, October 1929, began a fall that erased about 90% of stock values by July 1932.
Gartner's Jackie Fenn drew her hype cycle in 1995, five stages from Technology Trigger to Plateau of Productivity, offered as a framework for how expectations about new technologies move.
Netscape's shares, offered at $28 on 9 August 1995, closed at $58.25 on their first day, valuing it at $2.9 billion and kicking off investment in Internet companies.
Nasdaq peaked at 5,048 on 10 March 2000, then lost 78 percent by October 2002, erasing every gain of the dot-com bubble.
Initial coin offerings, sales of newly created digital tokens, raised billions of dollars in 2017 for ventures with little history, then contracted sharply when crypto prices fell from early 2018.
On 30 May 2023 Nvidia briefly became the first chipmaker worth $1 trillion, its market value rising as high as $1.036 trillion before closing near $990 billion.
Big technology firms planned roughly $400 billion of capital spending in 2025, mostly AI infrastructure; Goldman Sachs put the largest cloud providers' outlay about 70 percent above 2024.
Nvidia's pledge in 2025 to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI while supplying its chips raised concern that the money could return to Nvidia through OpenAI's chip purchases.
In 2025 OpenAI chief Sam Altman compared AI investment to the 1990s dot-com bubble and said some investors would lose substantial money.
On 15 October 2026 technology stocks worldwide sold off on worries about borrowing costs, Chinese competition and whether AI investment would pay off, with Nvidia down 10% from its record.
